h: Leicester tips before the first strike
p: Leicester railway station is around a ten-minute walk from the Clock Tower, and the city's main bus station, Haymarket, is practically next door, so it's easy to reach without a car. That's handy for a night out, as you can enjoy a drink or two with your game and get home without worrying about parking.

A few pointers for the night. Bring photo ID if you look young, as bar-led venues commonly check. Book a lane ahead for weekend evenings, and if your group is bigger than six, think about two lanes so turns keep moving. Swap teams halfway through to stop any one person running away with the scoreboard.

If you're arriving early, the Curve theatre in the Cultural Quarter is a short walk away, putting on big touring musicals and its own productions. The Phoenix arts centre nearby shows independent films and hosts exhibitions. Over on the edge of the centre, Abbey Park has a lake, gardens and the ruins of the medieval abbey, a lovely spot for a stroll on a sunny afternoon.

Sports fans will know Leicester is home to both the Foxes, who famously won the Premier League in 2016, and the Leicester Tigers rugby club at Welford Road. If there's a home game on, expect the city to be busy, so get your lane booked well ahead and plan your journey in good time.
